numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For length-2 inputs where one array is constant, stats.pearsonr returns statistic=0.0 and pvalue=1.0 instead of nan, while also emitting a ConstantInputWarning. The n==2 early-return path computed sign products of differences, which does not yield NaN for constant input.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: stats.pearsonr should return np.nan for both statistic and pvalue (PearsonRResult(statistic=nan, pvalue=nan)) with a ConstantInputWarning, as the documentation states; for n==2 non-constant inputs the statistic should be exactly 1.0 or -1.0.
trigger_conditions: one or more inputs are constant, e.g. x=[1, 1]
oracle_clues: documentation states np.nan is returned for constant inputs and that r is exactly 1 or -1 when n==2
test named test_length_two_constant_input added in scipy/stats/tests/test_stats.py using xp_assert_equal or xp_assert_allclose
ConstantInputWarning is raised in the buggy case

category_specific_evidence: PR body: stats.pearsonr([1, 1], [2, 3]) returned PearsonRResult(statistic=0.0, pvalue=1.0) before the fix, but the documented expected outcome is statistic=nan, pvalue=nan for a constant input array of length two.
Documentation promise cited in PR: for n==2 the correlation r takes only exact 1 and -1 values, and the constant-input case should return np.nan with a ConstantInputWarning.
Discussion: a user noted that 0.9999 vs 1.0 matters because the docs promise only 1 and -1 for r when n==2; the fix comment says to return exact 1.0 or -1.0 values for the n==2 case.
Diff removed the special-case n==2 branch that computed r as sign(x[1]-x[0])*sign(y[1]-y[0]) with pvalue=ones, which bypassed the constant-input handling.
New test test_length_two_constant_input uses x=[0.667, 0.667], y=[0.123, 0.456] and expects both r and p to be nan under pytest.warns(ConstantInputWarning).
Commit history mentions using xp.round instead of xp_sign and xp.where instead of element reassignment, and skips JAX tests because JAX does not allow item assignment.
reproduction_risks: The n==2 path had a regression from a side effect of an earlier change (#9562), so reproduction must cover n==2 with a constant input in one vector.
JAX backend is skipped for these tests because it does not allow item assignment; reproduction on jax.numpy may not be applicable.
Expected r values of exactly 1.0 or -1.0 for n==2 may fail if rounding is not applied, as the discussion notes 0.9999 can appear.
